reviewer_verifications: The deviation's reasoning is sound and reproduces: Decimal('5.610000000000001')/Decimal('6.6')-1 = -14.99999999999998484...%, and an independent Fraction(str(x)) oracle agrees on all 8 cases in the new parametrize.

Implementer's mutation claim confirmed exactly: floored-trigger -> 3 failed, all three in test_a_non_cent_price_is_judged_against_the_exact_level; price-snapped-to-cent -> 3 failed, likewise. Also re-ran nearest-cent (7), raw binary product (6), Decimal(x) not str (9), strictly-past (12), widened-a-cent (19), hard-coded -15 (2) - all red.

Conversion path clean on every operand probed: mae_pct as int (-15, -5), -33.3, -99.99, -0.1; entry 1e27/1e300/1e-299; int entry price; str(np.float64(3.2044)) is still '3.2044' under numpy 2.x. Default prec=28 cannot flip a comparison because a float's str is at most 17 significant digits.
T58 and T59 genuinely dissolved, verified through propose: entry 0.03 / -15% fires at 0.0255 and not at 0.026; entry 1e27, 1e30, 1e300 all produce a card, no traceback.
Docs honest: ARCHITECTURE.md:176-188 and README.md:73 assert no equivalence and no printed level.
reviewer_notes_routed_to_debt: The pinning comment at tests/test_allocator.py:806-808 has two wrong numbers: 5.610000000000001 is math.nextafter(5.61, 10), i.e. exactly one ULP up, NOT 5.61*(1+1e-15) which is ~7 ULP; and the stated loss -14.999999999999982% should be -14.99999999999998485%. A future reader checking the construction in a REPL gets a different number and may think the case is stale. -> folded into the R9 repair.
A stale docstring survives at tests/test_allocator.py:585 - 'The comparison is against the trigger price the card prints' - the card prints no trigger price now. -> folded into the R9 repair.
Setting the decimal context to prec=6 inside _past_threshold leaves 184 passed; getcontext().prec is process-global and mutable by any other library. -> T61.

A NaN price now raises decimal.InvalidOperation from the <= where the old float compare silently emitted a card with nan%. Unreachable from the shipped path (signals.monitor_inputs filters with pd.notna, NaN entry_price is caught by _entry_price's > 0). -> T61.
T58/T59 blocks carry their update in place but still read [status: todo] in their headers -> orchestrator bookkeeping, fixed this round.

findings.claim: The repair made off-cent prices fire, but the card still prints the price at two decimals, so a newly-reachable DECIDE card states a price that rounds *above* the threshold it claims the position is past — the card contradicts its own numbers and `details` disagrees with the reason text.
findings.evidence: kuroshio/core/allocator/engine.py:264 interpolates `_price_phrase(price, asof)` (engine.py:27-38, `f"at {price:.2f}"`) while engine.py:257 now compares the unrounded `price`. Entry 1.10, price 0.935 (the exact -15% level) fires and the card reads: `LOSER is -15.0% from your entry price of 1.10, at 0.94 — at or past your IPS max adverse excursion of -15.0%.` 0.94 from 1.10 is -14.55%, i.e. the two numbers the card prints refute the verdict printed beside them. `details` says `{'price': 0.935, ...}` — it does not agree with the text. Same shape at entry 0.30 / price 0.255 -> `at 0.26` (-13.3%). Both were NO CARD at 048bfd8 (floored level 0.93 / 0.25), so this card shape is introduced by this repair, not pre-existing. Not T60: that is scoped to penny names printing identically to the entry and asserts the numbers behind it are right; here the entry is $1.10 and the printed price rounds the wrong way across the threshold. Same user-visible contradiction class R7 was escalated for, reintroduced through the display path. Nothing pins it: tests/test_allocator.py:816 asserts only `bool(cards) is fires` and never the reason or details of an off-cent card; every reason/details assertion in the suite uses cent-grid 100.00/80.00. Mutation proof of the gap: rewriting engine.py:264 so the off-cent card names the entry price as the price it read leaves all 184 tests green.
findings.repro: propose([Holding(ticker='LOSER',weight=.05,score=.5,entry_price=1.10)],[],IPS(),'us',prices={'LOSER':0.935}) -> reason 'LOSER is -15.0% from your entry price of 1.10, at 0.94'. Orchestrator-verified for 1.10/0.935, 0.30/0.255 and 3.77/3.2044.
findings.acceptance: An off-cent DECIDE card prints a price consistent with the comparison that fired it (either at a precision that survives the level, or the price is not restated), and at least one test asserts the full `reason` string and `details` for a non-cent case such as entry 1.10 / price 0.935 and entry 3.77 / price 3.2044 — so the mutant above goes red. `details['price']` and the number in the reason must denote the same value.
findings.route_reason: Merged as named debt at the human's direction (option B at the round-4 circuit breaker). Folded into T60 and raised to P1: R9 and T60 are the same defect - the shared _price_phrase precision - and T60 already owned the thesis-card coupling. The verdict is correct in every case; a restated number beside it is not.
